title: Tautological rings and motivic structures in the cohomology of moduli of stable curves
summary: Build the moduli-specific algebra of tautological rings and semi-tautological extensions, its finite-generation and boundary-induction tools, and the geometric Chow–Kunneth arguments needed in genus seven. Combine an all-characteristic genus-four point-count sieve with equivariant stable-graph assembly to establish odd vanishing through nine. Plan the cusp-decorated graph calculations and realization classification in degrees thirteen, fourteen and fifteen, with explicit proof gates for descent, stack comparisons and finite computational certificates.
readme: This roadmap plans tautological and cusp-generated cohomology of stable curve moduli, with the genus-four point-count input and corrected genus-seven geometric gates. Rational coefficients, stable pairs, codimension/Tate conventions and the distinction between open and proper moduli are mandatory. All targets are detailed in the accompanying reader. Planning is complete; the packet explicitly records unresolved source proofs, stack supplier extensions, descent and finite certificates. No implementation or unconditional proof-closure claim is made.

stages.title: Tautological operations and cusp realizations
stages.description:
**Tautological Chow and cohomology rings.** For all stable pairs take the least system of unital graded rational Chow subalgebras R*(Mbar_g, n) closed under proper forgetting and clutching pushforward and the corresponding defined pullbacks and relabellings. The usual equivalent decorated-stable-graph description uses marking psi classes, vertex kappa classes and gluing. Put R*(M_g, n)=image of restriction and RH*=image under the cycle map. Cohomological degree is twice Chow codimension.

**Kappa classes of pointed curves.** For a stable forgetful map pi:Mbar_g, n+1→Mbar_g, n define kappa_a=pi_*(psi_(n+1)^(a+1)) for a≥0. Use the imported marking cotangent line and imported Hodge bundle E=f_*omega, retaining their forgetting corrections. Lambda_j means c_j(E); no new Hodge bundle is constructed.

**The stable-pair induction order.** For pairs of natural numbers define (g′, n′)≺(g, n) iff g′≤g, 2g′+n′≤2g+n, and the pairs differ. Restrict to 2g−2+n>0 when using moduli. Use integer d=3g−3+n. The order is well founded by lexicographic descent of (g,2g+n).

**Pure-weight boundary exact sequences.** For a stable pair with D the normalized boundary, there are exact sequences H^(k−2)(D)(−1)→H^k(Mbar_g, n)→W_k H^k(M_g, n)→0 and H_k(D)→H_k(Mbar_g, n)→W_(−k)H_k^BM(M_g, n)→0. The first arrow is the sum of finite Gysin maps with graph-automorphism invariants; H_k^BM(U)=H^(2d−k)(U)(d).

**Cusp realizations on genus-one moduli.** Identify S12=H11(Mbar_1,11) and S16=W15 H15(M_1,15) with the rank-two level-one parabolic realizations of cusp forms of weights12 and 16. L=Q(−1)=H2(P1), geometric Frobenius q. S12 has Hodge types(11,0),(0,11); S16 has(15,0),(0,15). General S_r has rank 2 dim S_r(SL2Z), rather than always rank two.

stages.title: Dimension bounds and finite odd-degree bases
stages.description:
**Virtual cohomological dimension bounds.** Ordinary rational H^i(M_g, n) vanishes for i>4g−5 when g≥2, n=0 and for i>4g−4+n when g≥1, n≥1. These are rational bounds obtained from mapping-class-group virtual cohomological dimension, not statements that the stack itself has no stabilizers.

**Vanishing in top virtual dimension.** H^(4g−5)(M_g)=0 for g≥2, and H^(4g−3)(M_g,1)=0 for g≥1, with rational coefficients. No analogous blanket claim for n≥2 is included.

**Low compact-support and Borel–Moore vanishing.** For g≥1, H_c^k(M_g, n)=0 if k<2g for n=0 or1, and if k<2g−2+n for n≥2. Equivalently H_k^BM(M_g, n)=0 in these ranges. Interpret only stable pairs.

**Arbarello–Cornalba boundary injection.** If H_c^k(M_g, n)=0, restriction H^k(Mbar_g, n)→H^k(Dnorm) is injective. Dnorm is the disjoint union of normalized one-edge boundary quotient stacks, with rational graph-automorphism invariants.

**Arbarello–Cornalba odd-degree induction.** For an odd k≥1, suppose every odd q≤k vanishes for all stable g≥1 pairs with max(2g,2g−2+n)≤k. Then every odd q≤k vanishes for every stable pair, with genus-zero even cohomology supplied separately. This is a sufficient finite base region.

**Keel presentation in genus zero.** For n≥3, rational cycle class CH*(Mbar_0, n)→H^(2*)(Mbar_0, n) is an isomorphism, generated by boundary divisors with the symmetry, four-label cross-ratio and incompatible-boundary product relations; H^odd=0.

**Vanishing in degrees one, three and five.** H^k(Mbar_g, n)=0 for k∈{1,3,5} and all stable pairs.

**Lower-genus polynomial-count base ranges.** The compact stacks have polynomial point counts over every finite field for g=1, n≤10; g=2, n≤7; and g=3, n≤5. The needed equivariant extensions satisfy g′≤3 and 2g′+n′≤11, with genus-zero all n. Keep the polynomial coefficients and symmetric actions from their respective source computations.

**Vanishing in degree seven.** For every stable pair H7(Mbar_g, n)=0.

**Odd vanishing through nine in genus at most three.** For every stable g≤3 pair, H^q(Mbar_g, n)=0 for odd q≤9.

stages.title: Genus-one pure cohomology and symplectic systems
stages.description:
**Symplectic local systems on curve moduli.** For g≥1 on smooth M_g, let V=R1 f_*Q for its universal curve, rank 2g with alternating cup pairing V⊗V→Q(−1). For a partition lambda of length≤g define V_lambda by the irreducible symplectic highest-weight summand in tensor/Schur constructions, with central weight |lambda| and Tate factors fixed by contractions. For g=4 this is BFP’s V_lambda; T_lambda denotes a Specht module and is a different object.

**Pure cohomology of smooth genus-one moduli.** For k>0, n≥k, W_k H^k(M_1, n)≅S_(k+1)⊗T_(n−k+1,1^(k−1)). Its cusp multiplicity is binomial(n−1, k−1). Pullbacks from k-subsets containing a fixed marking give a free family of copies of S_(k+1). It vanishes for n<k; degree 0 is Q separately.

**Even genus-one cohomology is tautological.** For every n≥1, all even cohomology H^(2r)(Mbar_1, n) is tautological. Its ring is generated by boundary divisor and higher boundary-stratum classes with the unit; cotangent classes are rational boundary combinations.

**Stable range and coarse cohomological bound.** For g≥2, ordinary H^k(M_g, n) is tautological if k≤(2g−2)/3. Also H^k(M_g, n)=0 for k>4g−4+n. Use these deliberately nonsharp bounds in the finite-generation argument.

stages.title: Semi-tautological extensions and finite generation
stages.description:
**The marking subspaces Phi and Psi.** On a stable smooth pair, Phi^k=sum_i pi_i* W_k H^k(M_g, n−1), where pi_i* here denotes pullback, and Psi^k=sum_i psi_i·Phi^(k−2), with the resulting Tate twist understood in realizations. A sum uses only stable forgetful targets; if there are none it is zero. Degrees below zero give zero.

**The local-system marking quotient.** For g≥2, W_k H^k(M_g, n)/(Phi^k+Psi^k)≅⊕_(|lambda|=n) W_k H^(k−n)(M_g, V_lambda)⊗T_(lambda^transpose). If n>0 and n≥k, W_k H^k(M_g, n)=Phi^k. Partitions have length≤g; the zero and unit cases are handled separately.

**Genus-two even pure and compact cohomology.** For 0≤r≤10 and every n≥0, W_(2r)H^(2r)(M_2, n)=RH^(2r)(M_2, n); consequently H^(2r)(Mbar_2, n)=RH^(2r)(Mbar_2, n).

**Semi-tautological extensions.** An STE is a system of unital graded Q-subalgebras S*(Mbar_g, n) containing RH*, stable under all relabelling and forgetting pullbacks and all clutching pushforwards, including external products on factors. Do not impose forgetting pushforward or clutching pullback in its definition. The STE generated by a family is the intersection of systems containing it; motivic means sub-Hodge structures and G_Q-stable spaces in the respective realizations.

**The filling criterion.** Let S be an STE and fix stable(g, n), k≥0. Suppose S^q(Mbar_g′, n′) surjects onto W_qH^q(M_g′, n′)/(Phi^q+RH^q) for the current triple and every stable smaller pair, 0≤q≤k, with 2d′−q≤2d−k. Then S^k(Mbar_g, n)=H^k(Mbar_g, n). This strengthened sufficient criterion includes same-degree forgetting cases; the printed q≤k−2 condition alone is false.

**Odd-marking reduction in genus two.** For odd n≥1 and k≥2, the STE generated by H^k(Mbar_2, n−1), H^(k−2)(Mbar_2, n−1) and H^(k−2)(Mbar_1, m) for 1≤m≤n+2 contains H^k(Mbar_2, n).

**Cusp-generated extensions and all tautological operations.** The STE generated by H11(Mbar_1,11) contains every H11(Mbar_g, n) and every H13(Mbar_1, n), and is closed also under forgetting pushforward and clutching pullback. The same operation-closure argument applies to an STE generated by rational subspaces of genus-one cusp-form realizations, with Hodge/Galois closure when required.

**Finite generation in each cohomological degree.** For every k≥0 the STE generated by all H^(k′)(Mbar_g′, n′) with 0≤k′≤k, g′<3k′/2+1, n′≤k′ and 4g′−4+n′≥k′ contains H^k(Mbar_g, n) for every stable pair. The set of seed triples is finite; k=0 follows from the units already in RH.

**Homological finite generation.** For fixed k≥0 a finitely generated STE has S^(2d−j)(Mbar_g, n)=H^(2d−j)(Mbar_g, n) for every0≤j≤k. One sufficient finite seed region consists of stable g≥1 pairs with n≤1,2g≤k or n≥2,2g−2+n≤k; at each take the entire groups H^(2d−j), for 0≤j≤min(k,2d), together with the tautological system. Ordinary H_j has the additional(d) duality twist. These coarse bounds are derived from BM vanishing, not displayed in Remark 3.3.

**Finitely many simple realization types per degree.** For each fixed k only finitely many simple rational Hodge structures, respectively simple Q_l[G_Q]-representations, occur in H^k(Mbar_g, n)^ss over all stable pairs.

**Top-heaviness and growth below the middle.** Let S be an STE on Mbar_g, n and let d=3g−3+n. For a tautological ample divisor a, cup product by a^(d−k) gives an injection S^k→S^(2d−k) for 0≤k≤d. Cup product by a gives an injection S^k→S^(k+2) for k<d, so dimensions are nondecreasing toward the middle separately in even and odd degree.

stages.title: Chow–Kunneth generation and pure algebraicity
stages.description:
**The Chow–Künneth generation property.** A smooth finite-type algebraic stack X/k stratified by quotient stacks has CKgP if, for every finite-type algebraic stack Y/k stratified by quotient stacks, the ungraded rational exterior product A_*(X)⊗Q A_*(Y)→A_*(X×Y) is surjective. Y need not be smooth or proper; the universal quantifier is essential.

**Permanence of Chow–Künneth generation.** Within smooth finite-type stacks stratified by quotient stacks, CKgP passes to opens, to proper surjective targets along maps representable by DM stacks, and from all pieces of a finite stratification to their union. It is equivalent along affine bundles, passes to Grassmann bundles, and holds for BGL_r, BSL_r and BPGL_r.

**Chow–Künneth generation makes pure cohomology algebraic.** Let X be open in a smooth proper DM stack Xbar/C, with pure dimension d and CKgP. For every r the cycle class A_(d−r)(X)→W_(2r)H^(2r)(X)(r) is onto. W_kH^k(X)=0 for odd k, and its even part is Hodge–Tate. Over a finitely generated characteristic-zero field the analogous l-adic statement uses a smooth proper compactification and the corresponding weight/cycle comparison.

**Known low-genus Chow–Künneth ranges.** For g=0 take every stable n; for g=1,2,3,4,5,6 take n≤10,10,11,11,7,5 respectively. Then M_g, n has CKgP and A*=R*. Consequently W_kH^k=RH^k, and odd W_kH^k and Gr_k^W H_c^k both vanish. The genus-seven extension n≤3 is supplied by TC.6, not assumed here.

stages.title: Tetragonal covers and gonality strata
stages.description:
**Gonality strata in genus seven.** Inside smooth M_7, n let M^≤a_7, n be the locus of curves with geometric gonality at most a; let M^a denote exact gonality a. Genus seven has gonality≤5. Use the closed≤3 locus, the exact tetragonal stratum≤4 minus≤3, and the open pentagonal stratum M^circle=M^5. Markings are ordered distinct smooth sections.

**The low-gonality genus-seven locus.** For n≤14, M^≤3_7, n has CKgP and every Chow class on M7, n supported on that closed locus is tautological.

**Tetragonal Hurwitz data and Casnati–Ekedahl bundles.** Let H^diamond_4,7, n parametrize finite flat degree-four maps C→P1 from smooth genus-seven curves of gonality at least4, with n distinct ordered points, modulo target PGL2. Its Casnati–Ekedahl data are rank-three E and rank-two F of degree 10 on the universal P1, with detE≅detF and C cut out by two relative quadrics in P(E dual). Retain target automorphisms and the determinant comparison.

**Tetragonal splitting strata.** In H^diamond_4,7,0 take X with E=O(3)⊕O(3)⊕O(4), F=O(5)⊕O(5) or O(4)⊕O(6); Sigma2 with E=(2,4,4), F=(4,6); Sigma3 with E=(2,3,5), F=(4,6). The remaining hyperelliptic splitting locus is removed. Subscript n means pullback to n distinct markings.

**Casnati–Ekedahl pushforward is tautological.** For any genus g≥2 in the tetragonal construction, define the same Hurwitz stack with rank 3 E and rank 2 F both of degree g+3. A class in the image A*((P E dual)^n)→A*(H^diamond_4, g, n) pushes forward under the proper forgetting map to a tautological class on M_g, n minus its gonality≤3 locus. The genus-seven instance has degree 10.

**The open tetragonal stratum with at most three marks.** For 0≤n≤3, X_n has CKgP and restriction A*((P E dual)^n)→A*(X_n) is onto.

**Chow generation on the special tetragonal strata.** For ell=2,3 and n≤3, the Chow ring of Sigma_(ell, n) is generated over A*(Sigma_ell) by the n base and projective hyperplane classes z_i, zeta_i; Sigma_(ell, n) has CKgP. The ambient restriction A*((P E dual)^n)→A*(Sigma_(ell, n)) is onto.

**Tetragonal Chow generation and support theorem.** For n≤3, H^diamond_4,7, n and the exact tetragonal locus have CKgP; ambient restriction onto A*(H^diamond_4,7, n) is surjective. Every class on M7, n supported on its tetragonal locus after removing≤3 is tautological.

stages.title: Orthogonal geometry and the corrected Mukai gates
stages.description:
**Universal maximal-isotropic Chow generation.** For a split nondegenerate10-dimensional quadratic space over C, fix one connected component OG+(5,10). The quotient[OG+/SO10] is BP for its maximal-isotropic parabolic, with Levi GL5 and split unipotent radical of dimension 10. It has CKgP and rational Chow ring Q[c1(U),…, c5(U)]. On BP the standard quadratic bundle fits0→U→V→U dual→0; do not require an equivariant direct-sum splitting.

**Orthogonal Grassmann fibre powers.** For n≥1 and the universal oriented quadratic bundle over BSO10 with split rank-ten model, the n-fold fibre product of the fixed maximal-isotropic component has CKgP; its Chow ring is generated by the Chern classes of U1,…, Un. The relative-bundle step requires an oriented nondegenerate quadratic form and the chosen component, and a proved rational Chow generation theorem for such bundles; underlying vector-bundle triviality alone does not trivialize the form.

**Mukai central lift and moduli comparison.** For the smooth pentagonal genus-seven linear-section incidence I_n in the spinor embedding OG+⊂P(S+), S+ has rank 16 and the action is Spin10, not SO10. Construct[I_n/Spin10] and its central rigidification by the projectively ineffective Z(Spin10)=mu4. Prove the comparison of the resulting effective quotient[I_n/PSO10] with the actual stack M^circle_7, n, preserving precisely curve automorphism groups and all marking-forgetting maps. A residual gerbe description must name its band and any remaining stabilizers.

**Mukai bundle descent and rational transfer.** On the corrected lifted incidence, compute the mu4 central characters of S+, each tautological point line L_i, Q_n and the rank(7−n) subbundle E_n. Descend only zero-character combinations, or tensor by a specifically constructed cancelling line with its descent datum. Prove the resulting rational Chow and cohomology transfers to M^circle_7, n, including exterior products with every test stack for CKgP; keep character-zero Chow identities compatible with forgetting markings.

**Marked spinor incidence model.** On the Spin10 lift, let Z_n⊂(OG+)^n be the locus where the sum of the n tautological lines injects into S+. Put Q_n=coker(⊕L_i→S+), rank 16−n. For 0≤n≤4 use the subspace Grassmannian Gr^sub_(7−n)(Q_n), equivalently the supplier’s rank-nine quotient Grassmannian Gr_9(Q_n). Its universal kernel E_n has rank 7−n; its inverse image in S+ is the desired rank-seven subbundle containing the marked lines. Remove the nonsmooth-section locus. Gonality5 ensures independence of the marked canonical points. Transfer to M^circle_7, n requires both Mukai gates; the orthogonal fibre-power Chow argument applies only for n≥1.

**Tautological Chern identities on the corrected model.** For n≤4, after the Mukai descent gate, express the Chern classes of pulled-back U_i, L_i and E_n in kappa, psi and Hodge classes. Upstairs, U_i is determined by the rank 5 quadratic-kernel construction for omega(−sigma_i); L_i has c1=−psi_i in the source’s compatible linearization, and 0→⊕L_i→E_Hodge dual→E_n→0 has ranks n,7,7−n. Any central-cancelling twist changes these formulas and must be explicitly accounted for.

**Genus-seven Chow–Künneth generation and tautological Chow ring.** For 0≤n≤4, the pentagonal locus M^circle_7, n has CKgP and A*=R* once the corrected quotient and transfer gates are proved. For 0≤n≤3, M7, n itself has CKgP and A*(M7, n)=R*(M7, n). These are targets whose proof route is blocked by G-mukai and G-orthogonal; this packet does not certify the printed quotient proof.

stages.title: Hyperelliptic counts and the quadric sieve
stages.description:
**Hyperelliptic binary-form quotient.** For g≥2 over Z[1/2], present H_g as the quotient of squarefree binary forms of degree 2g+2 by the standard Arsie–Vistoli change-of-variables group. Its rational-point mass is the number of such forms divided by the connected group order(q²−1)(q²−q). This is a quotient-stack mass assertion, not an assertion that every curve has trivial automorphisms.

**The first hyperelliptic Frobenius moments.** For odd q, let a_C=q+1−#C(F_q) and sum with weight1/Aut(C) over H_g(F_q). For g≥2 the zeroth moment is q^(2g−1), every odd moment is zero, and the second moment is q^(2g)−1.

**Hyperelliptic counts with at most three marks.** For every finite field and g≥2: #H_g=q^(2g−1), #H_g,1=(q+1)q^(2g−1), #H_g,2=(q+2)q^(2g)−1, and #H_g,3=(q²+3q−1)q^(2g)−3q. Marks are ordered and distinct. The odd-characteristic proof uses the moments; the all-characteristics extension imports Bergström’s characteristic-two calculation.

**Canonical genus-four quadric incidence families.** For g=4 nonhyperelliptic C, the canonical image in P3 is a smooth complete intersection of a unique reduced irreducible quadric and a cubic modulo that quadric. Use three F_q quadric types Q_con, Q_nsp, Q_spl. Their equation spaces are A15 for cone cubics avoiding the vertex, and P15 for each smooth quadric. V^type_n parametrizes the equation plus n ordered distinct points lying on it; C^type_n is its universal complete-intersection curve, including singular and nonreduced fibres for the sieve.

**Counting genus-four curves by their quadric.** For every q and n≤3, the nonhyperelliptic moduli count is the sum over the three types of N^type_n(q)/a_type(q), where N counts smooth fibres in V^type_n. The automorphism orders are a_con=q7−q6−q5+q4, a_nsp=2(q6−q2), a_spl=2(q3−q)^2.

**Nonreduced fibres and terminating sieve bounds.** For the cone incidence, the reduced singular locus of a nonreduced fibre is P1 and has even Betti sum2, hence its signed coefficients vanish in degrees≥3. On Q_nsp the singular locus is a(1,1) curve, possibly with an isolated point, with even Betti sum≤4; on Q_spl it is a ruling or(1,1) curve, possibly with points, with even Betti sum≤5. Apply these to the finite inverse-zeta sieve; smooth fibres contribute1 and nonempty singular loci contribute0 in the full sum.

**Inverse zeta functions for the three quadric types.** For X=Q_con minus its vertex, Z_X(t)^−1=(1−qt)(1−q²t). For Q_nsp it is(1−t)(1−qt)(1+qt)(1−q²t); for Q_spl it is(1−t)(1−qt)^2(1−q²t). Signed configuration coefficients use one minus sign per Frobenius orbit, not per geometric point.

**Cone sieve coefficients.** For 0≤n, d≤3 the signed sieve coefficient S_d(C^cone_n) is the polynomial in the attached table, with p_r=1+q+…+q^r and qj meaning q^j. For the split marked rows, displayed S2, S3 and the n=3 S1 are their degree≥6 polynomial part with error o(q6) as q grows through prime powers; unmarked rows and the other marked S0, S1 formulas are exact. Cone and nonsplit tables are exact.

**Nonsplit-quadric sieve coefficients.** For 0≤n, d≤3 the signed sieve coefficient S_d(C^nonsplit_n) is the polynomial in the attached table, with p_r=1+q+…+q^r and qj meaning q^j. For the split marked rows, displayed S2, S3 and the n=3 S1 are their degree≥6 polynomial part with error o(q6) as q grows through prime powers; unmarked rows and the other marked S0, S1 formulas are exact. Cone and nonsplit tables are exact.

**Split-quadric sieve coefficients.** For 0≤n, d≤3 the signed sieve coefficient S_d(C^split_n) is the polynomial in the attached table, with p_r=1+q+…+q^r and qj meaning q^j. For the split marked rows, displayed S2, S3 and the n=3 S1 are their degree≥6 polynomial part with error o(q6) as q grows through prime powers; unmarked rows and the other marked S0, S1 formulas are exact. Cone and nonsplit tables are exact.

**Bounds for four or more singularities.** For each type and 0≤n≤2, sum_(d≥4) S_d(C^type_n)/a_type=o(q^((9+n)/2)). For n=3 it is B_type q6+o(q6) with B_type an integer. The same statements hold for the nontrivial marking twists used in TC.8.

**Signed four-point general-position count.** On P1×P1 over F_q, the signed Frobenius-stable degree-four configuration count with no two points on a ruling and not all on an irreducible(1,1) curve equals(q+1)^2 q²(q−1)^2=#(PGL2×PGL2)(F_q). The sign is(−1)^number-of-Frobenius-orbits; this is not the count of ordered four-tuples.

stages.title: Equivariant realizations and the graph transform
stages.description:
**Twists by permutations of markings.** For a partition lambda of n, choose sigma of that cycle type and descend M_g, n, Fbar_q with geometric Frobenius sigma F_q to M_g, lambda. Its rational objects are curves with ordered geometric marks permuted in the chosen cycles. Define compact and hyperelliptic twists with the same convention. Stack descent retains automorphisms and its trace comparison must be proved; a groupoid cannot be replaced by its set of isomorphism classes.

**Weight-graded equivariant Euler characteristic.** For an S_n-variety or admissible DM stack over C define e_c^(S_n)(X)=sum_(i, w)(−1)^i[Gr_w^W H_c^i(X)] in the Grothendieck ring of rational realizations with S_n action. When every contributing weight piece is Tate, write it as sum_j a_j L^j with a_j virtual rational S_n-representations. No positivity or individual purity is asserted for an open stack.

**The stable-graph transform.** For a stable collection V(g, n) of graded characteristic-zero S_n-representations, zero when2g−2+n≤0, define MV(g, n)=direct sum over connected stable graphs of total(g, n) of (tensor_v V(g_v, n_v))_(AutGamma). Automorphisms act by flag permutations and cohomological Koszul signs. There is no extra det(edge) twist in this ordinary free modular transform.

**Getzler–Kapranov boundary-character formula.** In the completed stable symmetric-function ring with filtration degree(p_i)=i, degree(h)=2 and Adams psi_r(h)=h^r, put Ch(V)=sum h^(g−1) ch(V(g, n)). Let Delta=sum_(r≥1) h^r[(r/2)∂²/∂p_r²+∂/∂p_(2r)]. Then Ch(MV)=Log(exp(Delta) Exp(Ch(V))). Here exp(Delta) is the ordinary operator exponential; Exp and Log are inverse plethystic operations. For point counts psi_r(q)=q^r. Positive-edge terms are Ch(MV)−Ch(V).

**Polynomial counts of open moduli and boundary.** If all compact Mbar_g′, n′ for(g′, n′)≼(g, n) have polynomial point counts over every finite field, then the Frobenius eigenvalues on H_c*(M_g, n) are integral powers of q; the open and boundary stacks have polynomial counts, and their equivariant weight Euler polynomials give the corresponding twisted counts. Do not infer semisimplicity of open Frobenius from eigenvalues.

**The genus-four Euler-characteristic normalization.** The ordinary Euler characteristic chi(M4,3)=−10. Equivariantly chi^(S3)(M4,3)=2s_(3)−6s_(2,1), with sign coefficient0. These are cohomological Euler characteristics of the moduli stack/coarse space with rational coefficients, not orbifold Euler mass.

**Equivariant hyperelliptic genus-four counts.** For every q, #^(S2)H4,2=(q9+q8−1)s2+q8 s_(1,1); #^(S3)H4,3=(q10+q9−q8−q)s3+(q9−q)s_(2,1), with zero sign coefficient.

**Sieve coefficients for nontrivial marking twists.** For marking cycle types(2),(2,1),(3), the attached cone, nonsplit and split tables give S_d for 0≤d≤3. Cone entries are exact; nonsplit and split entries are specified modulo o(q6), with unshown coefficients below degree 6. For the nonsplit(3) S0 the full exact expression is(q6−q²)p12 and its degree≥6 part is q18+q17+q16+q15. For split S0 rows the exact expressions are obtained from ordered cycle-type incidence; the displayed polynomials retain all nonzero degree≥6 terms. Here p_r=sum_(i=0)^r q^i.

stages.title: Genus-four counts and odd vanishing
stages.description:
**The genus-four approximate-count cutoff.** For 0≤n≤3, if #Mbar_4, n(F_(p^m))=P(p^m)+o(p^(m(9+2n)/2)) for a fixed prime p and polynomial P, then H9(Mbar_4, n)=0. Here d=9+n and s=9+2n; duality turns the high-odd vanishing k≥s into low-odd vanishing k≤9. An integral approximation with smaller error o(q^((9+n)/2)) supplies the exact-polynomial recognition input for smooth proper all-Z moduli.

**Genus-four boundary point counts.** For 0≤n≤3 and every q, #boundary M4, n is the polynomial with ascending coefficient list in the attached table. Its degree is8+n. Coefficients come from ordinary open boundary strata with their finite graph automorphism quotients.

**Polynomial counts of compact genus-four moduli.** For 0≤n≤3 and every finite field, #Mbar_4, n(F_q) is the polynomial with ascending integer coefficient list in the attached table. It has degree d=9+n, nonnegative coefficients and symmetry a_i=a_(d−i). The n=3 middle coefficient is10605.

**Polynomial counts of smooth genus-four moduli.** For 0≤n≤3 and every q, #M4, n(F_q) is the polynomial with ascending coefficient list in the attached table. It is the difference of closed and boundary polynomials. In particular the n=3 q3 coefficient is−11, correcting the q4 misprint in §10.1.

**Pure Tate cohomology in the compact genus-four range.** For n≤3, odd cohomology of Mbar_4, n vanishes and H^(2j) is a direct sum of a_(n, j) copies of L^j, with a_(n, j) the closed-count coefficient. This holds for rational Hodge structures and as actual G_Q-representations after the full all-Z comparison inputs. For the open stacks the displayed polynomials describe only the alternating compact-support realization class.

**Odd cohomology vanishes through degree nine.** For all stable pairs H^k(Mbar_g, n)=0 for odd k≤9. The cutoff is sharp uniformly in(g, n), because dim H11(Mbar_1,11)=2.

**Symmetric-group equivariant genus-four counts.** For n=2,3 the compact and open equivariant count polynomials are the Schur coefficient lists attached here, in ascending powers of q. For n=2 the basis is s2, s11, dimensions1,1; for n=3 it is s3, s21, s111, dimensions1,2,1. Compact coefficients are actual Betti representation classes, open coefficients virtual weight Euler classes.

**Local-system Euler traces on M4.** For each lambda listed, the alternating compact-support geometric-Frobenius trace on H_c*(M4, V_lambda) is the attached polynomial for every q. Its weight-Euler/Galois realization is obtained by replacing q with L with the same coefficients. The partitions have size≤3.

stages.title: Tautological even cohomology and homology
stages.description:
**Tautological cohomology through degree three.** For all stable pairs H^k(Mbar_g, n)=RH^k(Mbar_g, n) for 0≤k≤3. In particular H1=H3=0, H0=Q, and degree 2 is spanned by boundary, psi and Hodge divisor classes.

**All degree-four cohomology is tautological.** For every stable pair H4(Mbar_g, n)=RH4(Mbar_g, n), in cohomological grading.

**Degree-six cohomology in genus at least ten.** For g≥10 and every stable n, H6(Mbar_g, n)=RH6(Mbar_g, n).

**Tautological even homology through degree fourteen.** For every stable pair and every even 0≤k≤14, the complementary cohomology H^(2d−k)(Mbar_g, n) is tautological. Equivalently ordinary H_k is represented by tautological cycles, with the duality twist(d) understood. Negative cohomological degrees are zero.

**The complementary degree-fourteen Tate realization.** For all stable pairs, H^(2d−14)(Mbar_g, n)^ss is a finite direct sum of L^(d−7), as rational Hodge structures and as Q_l[G_Q]-representations. The multiplicity is zero if the degree lies outside0..2d.

**A finite criterion for all degree-six cohomology.** If RH6(Mbar_g, n)×RH^(2d−6)(Mbar_g, n)→Q(−d) is a perfect pairing for every stable g≤9, n≤6, then H6(Mbar_g, n)=RH6(Mbar_g, n) for all stable pairs. This is a conditional criterion; the finite perfectness calculation is not supplied.

stages.title: Cusp graphs and the exceptional genus-two bases
stages.description:
**Genus-two degree thirteen and fifteen realizations.** For every n≥0, W13 H13(M_2, n)^ss and H13(Mbar_2, n)^ss are sums of L S12; W15 H15(M_2, n)^ss and H15(Mbar_2, n)^ss are sums of L² S12 as Q_l[G_Q]-representations. Multiplicities can be zero. The Hodge version of degree 15 is proved geometrically in TC.12.

**Cusp-decorated stable graphs.** An omega-decorated stable graph has one specified genus-one vertex carrying a pullback of omega∈H11(Mbar_1,11) along the forgetful map that retains eleven selected flags, unit classes on other vertices, and additional named tautological decorations. Pushforward along its e edges, before extra decorations, is a morphism L^e S12→H^(11+2e)(Mbar_g, n). A graphical basis means a basis of this Hom multiplicity space together with the resulting isomorphism from its tensor product with L^e S12; it is not a basis of individual rational vectors. Omitted markings lie on the designated genus-one vertex only when this is explicitly the drawing convention.

**Cusp multiplicity basis on Mbar_(1,12).** H13(Mbar_(1,12)) is the direct sum of 11 copies of L S12, and the 11 one-edge maps specified by the source graph families form its multiplicity basis.

**Cusp multiplicity basis on Mbar_(1,13).** Fix labels{x, y,1,…,11}. H13(Mbar_1,13)≅(L S12)^429 has the following one-edge multiplicity basis, with all omitted labels on the genus-one side and p its attaching flag: (a) a rational tail bearing any three-element label set, decorated by omega on its eleven remaining flags (286); (b) a tail{y, i}, i∈{1,…,11}, and omega_x on the genus-one side (11); (c) a tail{x, j}, j≠x, and omega_i for any original label i∉{x, j} (132). Retained flags are ordered by the fixed label order followed by p.

**Cusp multiplicity basis on Mbar_(1,14).** Fix labels{x, y,1,…,12}. H13(Mbar_1,14)≅(L S12)^6006 has five one-edge multiplicity-basis families, with rational tail and all omitted labels on the genus-one side: (a) any four-label tail, decoration omega (1001); (b) any three-label tail, omega_l for any of the eleven remaining original labels l (4004); (c) tail{1, i}, 2≤i≤12, omega_xy (11); (d) tail{y, j}, j∈{1,…,12}, omega_xi for i∈{1,…,12} minus{j} (132); (e) tail{x, k}, k≠x, omega_ij for an unordered two-subset{i, j} of the other twelve original labels (858). The attaching flag is retained and ordered last.

**Cusp multiplicity basis on Mbar_(2,12).** H13(Mbar_(2,12)) is the direct sum of 264 copies of L S12, and the 264 one-edge maps specified by the source graph families form its multiplicity basis.

**The891-graph restriction matrix.** The891 two-edge cusp maps in CLP Figure 2 have a selected boundary-restriction matrix of rank 825. Its66-dimensional kernel is spanned by M_ij=R1(ij)+(1/24)R2(ij)+R3[i, j]+R3[j, i]−R4(ij)+(1/12)R5(ij), indexed by unordered pairs of distinct labels. These are relations among the selected restrictions, not yet relations among the global classes.

**The corrected unordered-pair representation.** The S12-module spanned by formal symbols M_ij is Ind_(S10×S2)^S12(sgn10⊠1), of dimension 66, and decomposes as T_(2,1^10)⊕T_(3,1^9), dimensions11 and 55. It is not induction from S10 alone, which has dimension 132.

**Boundary generation of H15 on Mbar_2,12.** H15(Mbar_2,12) is an actual direct sum of836 copies of L²S12, generated by the 891 two-edge cusp maps. Their global relation space has dimension 55.

**The adjacent genus-two exceptional bases.** The cusp STE generated by H11(Mbar_1,11) contains H13(Mbar_2,11) and H15(Mbar_2,13).

stages.title: Cusp homology and the realization classification
stages.description:
**Cusp generation of degree-thirteen homology.** For every stable pair the STE generated by H11(Mbar_1,11) contains H^(2d−13)(Mbar_g, n), equivalently the complementary cohomological realization of H_13.

**Two-cusp generation of degree-fifteen homology.** For every stable pair the STE generated by H11(Mbar_1,11) and H15(Mbar_1,15) contains H^(2d−15)(Mbar_g, n).

**Complementary odd-degree realizations.** For every stable pair, H^(2d−13)^ss is a sum of copies of L^(d−12)S12, and H^(2d−15)^ss is a sum of copies of L^(d−13)S12 and L^(d−15)S16, in both Hodge and Galois realizations. Multiplicities depend on the pair and vanish outside its cohomological range.

**Genus-two complementary-degree generation and degree-fifteen realizations.** For every n, with d=3+n, the STE generated by H11(Mbar_1,11) contains H^(2d−15)(Mbar_2, n), the complementary cohomology underlying degree-fifteen homology. By duality, H^15(Mbar_2, n)^ss is a sum of L²S12 in Hodge and Galois realizations. This does not assert STE generation of H^15 itself for all n.

**The oriented weight-fifteen boundary complex.** Let C^j_15(g, n)=⊕_(|EΓ|=j)(H15(Mbar_Γ)⊗det Q^EΓ)^AutΓ. For j=0 this is H15(Mbar_g, n). The differential is the signed sum of restrictions that add one edge, with its exterior orientation; write alpha=d0 and beta=d1 on Hodge type(15,0). Use compact normalized vertex factors, not open strata.

**Injectivity in the weight-fifteen row.** For g≥3, alpha:H15(Mbar_g, n)→C1_15(g, n) is injective.

**No Hodge type(15,0) in genus at least two.** For all g≥2, n, H^(15,0)(Mbar_g, n)=H^(0,15)(Mbar_g, n)=0.

**A geometric splitting of the genus-one seed.** In H15(Mbar_1,15), let V be the boundary-pushforward image and W=image(Hc15(M_1,15)→H15(Mbar_1,15)). Then H15=V⊕W in both Hodge and Galois realizations, W≅S16, and V^ss≅(L²S12)^186263.

**The cohomological realization classification.** For every stable pair H13(Mbar_g, n)^ss is a sum of L S12 and H14(Mbar_g, n)^ss is a sum of L7. For g≥2, H15(Mbar_g, n)^ss is a sum of L²S12. These hold as rational Hodge structures and as Q_l[G_Q]-representations.

**Realizations of genus-three moduli through eleven markings.** For n≤11, every H^k(Mbar_3, n)^ss is a finite direct sum of tensor monomials in L and S12 in Hodge and Galois realizations; equivalently the total semisimplified cohomology lies in the positive semiring generated by their realization classes.
